feedback: [APPLICABILITY] TRF-120-ShipShape: The shape targets every nltl:ship and unconditionally requires damping, water added mass, and thruster natural frequency, although the requirement applies only when thruster global natural frequencies are being estimated. Required change: Add a canonical applicability condition for the estimation activity and gate these mandatory constraints on that condition, rather than applying them to every ship. | [CARDINALITY] TRF-120-ShipShape / nltl:hasComponent: nltl:hasComponent has no sh:minCount, so a conforming applicable ship may contain no thruster body and consequently evade the mandatory ship-attachment-stiffness modelling constraint. Required change: Set sh:minCount 1 on nltl:hasComponent, with the existing thrusterBody node constraints applied to each component. | [LOGIC] TRF-120-ShipShape / nltl:hasComponent / nltl:hasNaturalFrequencyCalculationCase / nltl:vibrationDirection: The shape permits a single calculation case in either the longitudinal or transverse direction, but does not require coverage of both directions explicitly required by the requirement. Required change: Require at least one longitudinal calculation case and at least one transverse calculation case for each applicable thruster body, using separate direction-specific constraints or equivalent SHACL logic.

current_issues.problem: The shape targets every nltl:ship and unconditionally requires damping, water added mass, and thruster natural frequency, although the requirement applies only when thruster global natural frequencies are being estimated.
current_issues.required_change: Add a canonical applicability condition for the estimation activity and gate these mandatory constraints on that condition, rather than applying them to every ship.
current_issues.regression_guard: Preserve the ship target while ensuring non-estimating ships are not subjected to the estimation requirements.

current_issues.problem: nltl:hasComponent has no sh:minCount, so a conforming applicable ship may contain no thruster body and consequently evade the mandatory ship-attachment-stiffness modelling constraint.
current_issues.required_change: Set sh:minCount 1 on nltl:hasComponent, with the existing thrusterBody node constraints applied to each component.
current_issues.regression_guard: Preserve the thrusterBody ownership of shipAttachmentStiffness and require at least one represented thruster body when the requirement applies.

current_issues.problem: The shape permits a single calculation case in either the longitudinal or transverse direction, but does not require coverage of both directions explicitly required by the requirement.
current_issues.required_change: Require at least one longitudinal calculation case and at least one transverse calculation case for each applicable thruster body, using separate direction-specific constraints or equivalent SHACL logic.
current_issues.regression_guard: Retain the locked longitudinalDirection and transverseDirection controlled values and require both rather than replacing them with an unrestricted direction.

feedback: [WRONG_APPLICABILITY] MainShape/or branch 1/property nltl:hasCalculationCase: The conditional branch is activated by any ship-level nltl:hasCalculationCase, although that property is a generic calculation-case relationship and is not restricted to thruster global natural-frequency estimation. This can impose TRF-120 obligations for unrelated calculation cases. Required change: Use an applicability condition tied specifically to the represented thruster natural-frequency estimation, or introduce and use a canonical relationship that identifies that estimation; do not use generic nltl:hasCalculationCase as the sole trigger. | [WRONG_APPLICABILITY] MainShape/or branch 1/property nltl:hasComponent: sh:node on nltl:hasComponent validates every ship component as an nltl:thrusterBody with the required stiffness and longitudinal/transverse calculation cases. The requirement applies to thruster bodies, not to every component reachable through the generic hasComponent path, so unrelated ship components can cause false nonconformance. Required change: Select and validate only hasComponent values that are nltl:thrusterBody, using a qualified value shape or an equivalent component-type restriction, while leaving unrelated ship components unconstrained by TRF-120.

feedback: [LOGIC] TRF-120-ThrusterBodyShape / transverse hasNaturalFrequencyCalculationCase property: The transverse qualifiedValueShape only checks for nltl:vibrationDirection equal to nltl:transverseDirection and does not require the value to be an nltl:calculationCase or otherwise satisfy the calculation-case constraints. An unrelated node with that direction can therefore satisfy the transverse requirement. Required change: Make the transverse qualified value shape also require nltl:calculationCase and the applicable calculation-case direction constraint, preferably by reusing the same calculation-case node shape used by the longitudinal case.

current_issues.problem: The transverse qualifiedValueShape only checks for nltl:vibrationDirection equal to nltl:transverseDirection and does not require the value to be an nltl:calculationCase or otherwise satisfy the calculation-case constraints. current_issues.required_change: Make the transverse qualified value shape also require nltl:calculationCase and the applicable calculation-case direction constraint, preferably by reusing the same calculation-case node shape used by the longitudinal case.
current_issues.regression_guard: Continue requiring both locked nltl:longitudinalDirection and nltl:transverseDirection cases for each represented estimating thruster body.

feedback: [CARDINALITY] TRF-120-ShipShape nltl:thrusterNaturalFrequency property: The shape restricts thrusterNaturalFrequency to at most one ship-level quantity, although the requirement concerns natural-frequency estimates in both longitudinal and transverse directions. The candidate provides no way to represent or distinguish the two directional frequency results. Required change: Remove the single-value restriction and require distinct natural-frequency results for the longitudinal and transverse calculation cases, with each result associated with its corresponding direction.
